title: Nucleus and Binding Energy
notes: **Nucleus and Binding Energy:** This topic covers the fundamental concepts of nucleus and binding energy in the physics curriculum.
Understanding nucleus and binding energy is essential for solving problems and building higher-level mathematical skills.
Key definitions and theorems related to nucleus and binding energy should be memorized and practiced regularly.
confusion: ❌ Thinking nuclear mass equals sum of nucleons ✅ Nuclear mass is less than the sum of its constituents' masses; the difference is the mass defect, converted into binding energy (E = mc²).
❌ Misinterpreting binding energy per nucleon as total binding energy ✅ Binding energy per nucleon determines nuclear stability; higher values generally indicate a more stable nucleus.
❌ Confusing fusion and fission energy release ✅ Both processes release energy, but fusion involves combining light nuclei, while fission involves splitting heavy nuclei.
